title: Six-Dimensional Kissing Configurations with Q5 or R5 Cross Sections
content: Cohn and Rajagopal conjectured that no six-dimensional kissing configuration with Szöllősi's configuration Q5 or with their configuration R5 as a cross section can contain 72 or more points. We prove that such a configuration has at most 70 points, and we exhibit configurations with 64 points. The argument combines three ingredients: an elementary bound on the heights of points above a cross section in terms of its covering constant; a positive-kernel bound on each side of the section, together with its equality case; and explicit polar and deep-hole certificates. The upper bound 70 and a manual polar certificate also appear in a manuscript of Iuzhakov and Vetrov; we incorporate their certificate with attribution, so the proof of this bound and the 64-point constructions can be checked without exhaustive computation. The same method shows that every 72-point kissing configuration in R6 with a D5 or L5 cross section is isometric to one of the four classical configurations, and that a seven-dimensional kissing configuration with an E6 cross section has at most 126 points, with exactly two configurations attaining 126 up to isometry. We also prove explicit neighborhood bounds of 40, 72 and 126 in dimensions five, six and seven; for E6 the radius is \( \sqrt{113/448}-1/2>1/450 \).
